Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test testObjectCycle creates two objects that reference each other to exercise the object-cycle detection used by ToStringBuilder/ToStringStyle. After the cycle handling, it calls validateNullToStringStyleRegistry(), which asserts that ToStringStyle’s internal registry is null, i.e., that no ThreadLocal state remains and thus there is no risk of memory leaks.
- validateNullToStringStyleRegistry() does assertNull(ToStringStyle.getRegistry()).
- However, ToStringStyle.getRegistry() is implemented to never return null:
  - It returns REGISTRY.get() if present; otherwise it returns Collections.emptyMap().
- Therefore, even when the ThreadLocal has been removed (via unregister calling REGISTRY.remove() when the map is empty), getRegistry() returns an empty Map instead of null. This causes validateNullToStringStyleRegistry() to print the empty map and then fail the assertNull.
- This directly relates to the reported issue about ThreadLocals and memory leaks: the test is verifying that the ThreadLocal is fully cleared (observable via a null registry). The current implementation of getRegistry() masks that condition by returning a non-null empty map, breaking the test’s contract and obscuring the intended leak-prevention signal.
- The register/unregister logic itself correctly sets up the registry and removes the ThreadLocal when it becomes empty. The fault lies solely in getRegistry()’s return value semantics (returning an empty Map instead of null), which contradict the test’s expectation and the intended API contract used to detect cleanup.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
